silence.source_quote: If the family is unable to go, the ASHA should ensure that the ANM visits the sick newborn on a priority basis.
silence.timing_note: retry_after_hours (6) and max_retries (1) are a Day Three product decision (PLAN §4.6), not a WHO/HBNC citation — S5 sources only the escalation actor (ASHA/ANM home visit backstop), not the retry timing.

not_modelled.subject: Postpartum depression / thoughts of self-harm as a routable, clinically-assessed danger sign
not_modelled.reason: None of S1, S2, S4, S5, or S6 that were actually read contain a quotable danger-sign line for this. No threshold or route was invented; M_SELF_HARM exists only as an always-escalate safety net (rule M-SELF-HARM-01, route HUMAN_REVIEW_NOW) — the engine never claims to assess it.

not_modelled.subject: HBYC (Home Based Care for Young Child) day-count schedule
not_modelled.reason: A PDF was located but never scraped or verified against an official nhm.gov.in-hosted copy; HBYC also covers ages beyond the newborn (0–42 day) period this pack models.

not_modelled.subject: LaQshya discharge-readiness criteria
not_modelled.reason: The official LaQshya page describes the initiative's objectives, not a quotable discharge-readiness checklist or danger-sign list — no rule was extracted from it.

not_modelled.subject: The exact ASHA-facing danger-sign checklist form (S5 Annexure 1a/1b)
not_modelled.reason: S5 references 'Checklist for first Visit to the Newborn (Annexure 1a)' and 'Home visit form (Annexure 1b)' but the scraped markdown did not carry the annexure tables. This pack's newborn/maternal signs use the WHO NB/MAT tables instead and do not assume they are identical to Annexure 1a/1b.

not_modelled.subject: Mode-of-delivery-specific schedule adjustments (e.g. caesarean vs vaginal)
not_modelled.reason: None of the six sources read specify a distinct contact schedule by delivery mode.

disagreements.topic: Two different, non-identical follow-up schedules for two different actors
disagreements.reading_a: S1/S2 (WHO, clinic-facing): four contacts — within 24h, day 3 (48–72h), days 7–14, week 6.
disagreements.reading_b: S5 (India ASHA home-visit programme, institutional birth): six visits on fixed calendar days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42.
disagreements.applied: Both, run in parallel and never merged — ladder entries carry variant "WHO" (default) or "HBNC" (selectable by setting); the engine does not silently collapse the two schedules.

disagreements.reading_a: S1 Rec. 25 and S3 (IMCI "VERY SEVERE DISEASE"): fever >37.5°C is the emergency sign.
disagreements.applied: The lower, more cautious WHO PNC/IMCI threshold (>37.5°C) is the operative NB_FEVER cutoff, since S1 is the current (2022) primary guideline and S3 is WHO's own clinical-classification training material for the same age group. S4's 38°C threshold is noted here but not used.

disagreements.topic: "No spontaneous movement" (S1) vs the two-part stimulated/no-movement check (S3/S4)
disagreements.reading_a: S1 Rec. 25 lists only "no spontaneous movement" as the danger sign.
disagreements.reading_b: S3/S4 add the intermediate state "movement only when stimulated" as also an emergency sign.
disagreements.applied: NB_MOVEMENT_ABNORMAL follows S3/S4's more sensitive wording (moves only when stimulated, or not at all), since S1's wording is a shorter summary of the same underlying WHO construct.
